target_moa.text: Alirocumab is a human monoclonal antibody that binds to PCSK9; by inhibiting PCSK9 binding to LDL receptors it increases the number of LDLRs available to clear LDL, thereby lowering LDL-C.

citations.quote: Alirocumab is a human monoclonal antibody that binds to proprotein convertase subtilisin kexin type 9 (PCSK9).
By inhibiting the binding of PCSK9 to LDLR, alirocumab increases the number of LDLRs available to clear LDL, thereby lowering LDL-C levels.
Alirocumab is a fully human monoclonal antibody (IgG1 isotype) that targets proprotein convertase subtilisin kexin type 9 (PCSK9).

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>=5% and more frequent than placebo) are nasopharyngitis, injection site reactions, and influenza. Injection site reactions occurred in 7.2% vs 5.1% (placebo); allergic reactions 8.6% vs 7.8% (placebo); serious allergic reactions such as hypersensitivity, nummular eczema, and hypersensitivity vasculitis were reported in patients using PRALUENT.

citations.quote: The most commonly occurring adverse reactions (\geq 5\% of patients treated with PRALUENT and occurring more frequently than with placebo) are nasopharyngitis, injection site reactions, and influenza. (6.1)

Local injection site reactions including erythema/redness, itching, swelling, and pain/tenderness were reported more frequently in patients treated with PRALUENT (7.2% versus 5.1% for PRALUENT and placebo, respectively).
Allergic reactions were reported more frequently in patients treated with PRALUENT than in those treated with placebo (8.6% versus 7.8%).

Serious allergic reactions, such as hypersensitivity, nummular eczema, and hypersensitivity vasculitis were reported in patients using PRALUENT in controlled clinical trials [see Warnings and Precautions (5.1)].

summary.text: Praluent received a traditional (full) approval based on reduction in LDL-C, a surrogate endpoint that has been considered a surrogate for cardiovascular risk for decades, with the indication limited to high-risk patients (HeFH or clinical ASCVD) on maximally tolerated statins. The BLA received priority review via a priority review voucher and was reviewed by the EMDAC advisory committee (13-to-3 vote in favor); no accelerated approval or REMS was required.
